headline: Southborough set its FY27 tax rate while confronting a projected $1.4 million FY28 budget deficit and rising Neary School renovation costs.
synopsis: In November, Southborough set its fiscal year 2027 single tax rate at $14.54 while opening discussions on a challenging FY28 budget outlook. Municipal and school officials are reviewing two budget frameworks: a level-service model with a $1.4 million deficit requiring a Proposition 2 1/2 override, or a level-funded plan forcing departmental service cutbacks and the loss of 15 school positions. Meanwhile, architects reported that renovating Neary Elementary School will cost between $33 million and $40 million, ruling out an earlier $15 million target, even as the Neary roof replacement wrapped up nearly $1.6 million under budget. On the development front, the Planning Board continued reviewing traffic mitigation for the proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse on Coslin Drive. Additionally, the town received a state grant of up to $632,000 for Fayville Park improvements, while residents at a governance listening session strongly pushed back against consolidating the Senior Center with other town departments.

top_items.title: Town evaluates $1.4 million FY28 deficit and override
top_items.why: The Select Board reviewed preliminary FY28 budget models requiring either a $1.4 million Proposition 2 1/2 operating override or deep service reductions.
top_items.body: Town administration presented an early preview of the FY28 operating budget, outlining two scenarios for Town Meeting. Budget A maintains existing town services but carries a $1.4 million shortfall that would necessitate an operating override. Budget B limits funding to FY27 levels, requiring department heads to submit impact memos outlining cutbacks to public hours, staffing, and departmental services. The Select Board discussed whether to pursue a multi-year override and scheduled budget review hearings with major departments.

top_items.title: School Committee reviews preliminary 5.36% FY28 budget increase
top_items.why: School officials presented a preliminary $27.5 million operating budget, noting flat funding would require eliminating 15 staff positions.
top_items.body: District administrators presented a preliminary FY28 operating budget of $27,514,571, representing a 5.36% or $1.4 million increase driven by contractual salaries, transportation, and a 41% surge in out-of-district special education tuitions. The School Committee evaluated potential reduction scenarios to meet town guidance, which include trimming $616,411 to meet a 3% target or cutting $1.4 million and roughly 15 staff positions under level funding. A refined budget will be submitted in December following joint talks with the Select Board.

top_items.title: Neary School renovation estimates reach $33M to $40M
top_items.why: Architects demonstrated that renovating Neary School will cost $33 million to $40 million, concluding an earlier $15 million target is unfeasible.
top_items.body: Tappé Architects presented detailed cost breakdowns to the Elementary School Building Committee comparing required work against historical estimates. Baseline code upgrades and system modernizations are estimated at $32.9 million, while an addition and renovation plan addressing educational space and a regulation gym is projected at $39.8 million. Committee members asked the architects to integrate civil engineering and septic replacement costs into upcoming presentations to ensure complete figures are shared with the town.

top_items.title: Select Board approves single FY27 property tax rate
top_items.why: The Select Board voted 4-1 to maintain a uniform tax rate of $14.54 per thousand, rejecting residential and commercial exemptions.
top_items.body: During the annual tax classification hearing, assessors reported Southborough's total assessed value reached $4.072 billion, with the average single-family home value rising 3.7 percent to $1,027,800. The Select Board voted 4-1 to keep a unified single tax rate rather than a split commercial rate, resulting in an estimated 5.01 percent increase on the average single-family tax bill. The board also voted 5-0 against adopting residential or small commercial exemptions.

top_items.title: Neary roof replacement finishes $1.6M under budget
top_items.why: The Neary Elementary School roof replacement reached punch-list completion at $2.91 million, nearly $1.6 million below its original appropriation.
top_items.body: School administrators announced that the Neary Elementary School roof replacement has surpassed 97 percent completion and moved into punch-list closeout. Final project costs are projected at approximately $2.91 million, coming in almost $1.6 million below the $4.5 million borrowing authorization approved by Special Town Meeting in March 2026. The unused borrowing authorization will be retired to reduce municipal debt service.

top_items.title: Planning Board reviews traffic study for Coslin Drive Costco
top_items.why: Board members and residents examined intersection delays and neighborhood truck traffic generated by the proposed Costco warehouse.
top_items.body: Costco's project team presented an updated traffic impact study for the proposed 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-position fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive, incorporating feedback from MassDOT and peer reviewer Nitsch Engineering. The board and neighbors focused on regional traffic congestion, level-of-service failures at key intersections, and cut-through truck traffic on residential collector streets. Proposed developer mitigation includes repaving Coslin Drive and Crystal Pond Road, signal timing adjustments along Route 9, and a post-opening traffic review.

top_items.title: Residents push back against Senior Center department consolidation
top_items.why: Attendees at a municipal governance listening session voiced strong opposition to merging the Council on Aging with other departments.
top_items.body: During a public listening session hosted by the town's governance study consultant, senior center attendees strongly opposed potential proposals to consolidate the Council on Aging or Senior Center with recreation or youth services. Participants argued seniors represent roughly 20 percent of Southborough's population and require dedicated, distinct human services that would be compromised under a consolidated department. The consultant noted the community feedback and will include it in the final report to the Select Board in December.

top_items.title: Southborough awarded $632,000 state grant for Fayville Park
top_items.why: A state grant of up to $632,000 will fund half the cost of improvements at Fayville Memorial Park.
top_items.body: Town officials announced that Southborough received a state Land and Water Conservation Fund grant of up to $632,000 for the Fayville Memorial Park project, covering approximately half of its projected costs. The project includes a splash pad, dog park, walking trail, and accessibility upgrades, and will seek matching Community Preservation Act funds at the 2027 Annual Town Meeting. The Recreation Commission is coordinating with the Select Board and DPW to finalize roadway parking along Central Street.
